content.comment_body: Hello, I installed an [product_name] expansion module to my [product_name]. When viewing the analog channels, I notice a small input value appears even when nothing is connected. So, when I try to show the value on the display, it does not show zero. This occurs for both analog inputs. Is this expected behavior, or could there be an issue with my configuration? Regards, [user_name]
Welcome to the forum. I use a [product_name] base unit with multiple analog inputs, and when the inputs are left open, a small value (such as 2 units) is still displayed on those channels.

Thank you for your reply. Does this mean that the analog channels will always show a value even if there is no signal connected to them? For instance, if I want the display to show zero when no signal is present, do I need to subtract the default value from the displayed reading when the input is active? Best regards, [user_name]
I wouldn't be concerned about the small discrepancy, as it's only a minor error in percentage terms.
Alright, thank you for your assistance. Regards, [user_name]

analysis.insight_summary: Forum participants note that analog input channels on the [product_name] expansion module and base units can display a small non-zero value even without any signal connected. This occurrence is verified by another user, who has similar observations with their device. Users question whether the inputs should be calibrated to show a true zero value, whether this is standard device behavior, and express interest in display accuracy.
analysis.user_expectations: Users expect analog inputs to indicate exactly zero when there is no physical input signal. They are seeking accurate readings and want the display to accurately reflect the absence of a signal.
